reusable_cues.rationale: Derivation marker: the requirement that follows is presented as forced by the constraint just stated. Generalises across design reasoning.

source_text: The thing is, we can't necessarily afford to run things before the agent acts, which is why we need to create the ability to rewind.

fragments.text: The thing is, we can't necessarily afford to run things before the agent acts, which is why we need to create the ability to rewind.
fragments.target: the design space for agent action: pre-action simulation is unaffordable, so reversibility (rewind) is required instead
fragments.rationale: Joe derives a design requirement from an affordability constraint: if you cannot run/simulate outcomes before the agent acts, the only safety you can buy is the ability to rewind after. Reversibility substitutes for foresight. trail-enables-return covers the rewind requirement itself (traces that allow backtracking so mistakes are recoverable); the substitution move — rewind INSTEAD of pre-hoc gating/simulation — has no name, proposed as operator/if-you-cant-see-ahead-make-it-reversible (parent agent/trail-enables-return).

display_cues.text: run things before the agent acts

pattern_refs.rationale: The rewind ability Joe commissions is the pattern's conclusion: traces enabling backtracking so an agent that cannot pre-verify its acts can still recover from their outcomes.

pattern_rejections.reason: The consent-gate is the pre-hoc strategy Joe is explicitly pricing out: gating irreversible acts BEFORE they fire. Joe's constraint says pre-action checking is unaffordable here, so he buys reversibility instead — the boundary between the two patterns is exactly pre-hoc gate vs post-hoc rewind.
pattern_rejections.query: irreversible action, rollback, recover from agent mistakes
